reason: The primary CIF parses and symmetry-expands as a primitive ordered P-42_1m (No. 113) cell with a=b=9.15928 A, c=6.36918 A, 16 fully occupied atoms, Y10Sn6 = Y5Sn3 with Z=2; primitive standardization does not reduce it. Indexing is strong: 18/18 early lines give M(18)=217.8, all 74 detected peaks with prominence >1 are within 0.03 degrees of the tetragonal lattice, and 43 isolated lines refine with 0.00255 degrees RMS, leaving no important unindexed reflection. The instantiated CIF intensities match independently extracted profile amplitudes across 142 relevant line groups with correlation 0.99971 and relative RMS 0.0220; a constrained whole-profile fit gives Rwp=0.0443, close to the Pawley/profile lower bound 0.0399 and much better than the concrete site-swapped competitor (Rwp=0.1343). The trace's stoichiometrically valid direct-space searches also separate the submitted ordering (residual 0.00338) from the swapped runner-up (0.03787), other P-42_1m partitions (at least 0.143), and tested P42_12 candidates (at least 0.1669). Periodic geometry has no overlap or impossible shell: minimum Y-Sn, Y-Y, and Sn-Sn distances are 2.863, 3.181, and 4.387 A; conventional ionic bond-valence assignment is not applicable to this intermetallic. The explicit realization therefore has convergent diffraction support, while concrete ordering and symmetry alternatives are quantitatively rejected, so another attempt is unlikely to add a materially different viable candidate.
